Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Everything made sense in the end, but some of the information was very convoluted. For example, they did not tell us about what vaccines we should get until very late.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There is one week of introduction. Together with the other visiting students we attended introductory courses into the university and got to know each other. They also introduced us to resources to help us throughout our stay.

Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Living on campus at Barnard means that they have various apartments around the school. I lived in 616 W 116 which was pretty nice. What the school doesn't tell you is that after around a month you can change room, and those who tried could easily move into Sulzberger tower to get a single room.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: They have swipes and points. Swipes are for the dining halls and points are for the cafés on campus. We learned that you don't need more than 75 swipes, otherwise you will stress out about the dining halls in the end. And around a month before the semester ends there is a thing where people can donate their swipes if they have too many (which a lot of people do), so you can just use donated swipes if you need more in the end of the semester (I'm not sure if there is a maximum of donated swipes you can use).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
The housing situation is great and it is nicely close to the school. When you suggest housing you can suggest one person you want to live with, and I was really glad that me and another Dane (who barely knew each other) suggested each other. It makes the whole thing a lot more nice and chill, especially in the beginning. We also lived with three American girls, so it was nice to have another Dane in the apartment. 

The housing is really expensive, but much cheaper than the rest of New York, so I would say that it is a unique opportunity to get to live in NYC while not being totally ruined.

Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: In my experience, the classes were on the same level as in Denmark. However, they are way more generous with their grading.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I did English literature, so this might differ from other courses but depending on the subject, some of the tests we had to do were in hand. In one of my courses we were 15 people around a table, and then once in a while we would write about something that we had talked about. In another course we were around 60 and the professor would sometimes ask questions, but it was only a handful who participated. in two other courses we were around 50 in each, where the teacher would ask questions and would expect participation.

questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer:
Shakespeare II

Great Short Works of American Prose

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them. My teacher Rachel Eisendrath was particularly great. She taught the Shakespeare course. We went to Broadway to see Othello with Denzel Washington and Jake Gyllenhaal. Apparently that course goes to see a Shakespeare show every semester - this is really unique cause the tickets were wildly expensive, but an alumni had donated the tickets.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Ballet 30 for 30. You can get a ticket for 30 dollars if you are under 30 years old. 
Download the app TodayTix and go into lotteries where you can get a Broadway ticket for cheap. 
Your Barnard ID gives you free access to many museums across the city. 
Go to a Julliard performance for free. 
Lincoln Center for performing arts.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The American people are typically a bit younger than Danish university students, so that was a bit of a barrier.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are very open and kind.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
The process is a bit complicated before you go, but once you are at the school everything is sorted out for you.
Maybe a week before you come, ask for bedding. They will give you a bag with a duvet, covers and towels. (but they have a limited amount, so write to them).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can attend both classes at Barnard and Columbia. I would definitely recommend taking some classes at Columbia to get the full Ivy-league experience. It's such a beautiful university and the teachers are also excellent.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The city itself is amazing. The courses were also excellent.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Expenses.

Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
